chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: The 1950 European tour: five trumpets and Butch Ballard
summary: For Europe Duke took Ernie Royal as a fifth trumpet and Butch Ballard as extra drummer; Tyree stayed home and Jackson began the plunger role.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, definitely. Oh, sure, he was there when I got there. And when --
Uh-huh, when Shelton Hemphill died and he left, well, when we got ready to go to Europe, Francis Williams didn't go. He got Nelson Williams to go.

And Al Killian almost missed the boat, so -- Duke was kind of, you know, kind of [skimmish] about things like that -- he didn't know whether Al Killian was going to make it or not -- so he got Ernie Royal to come with us. So we had five trumpets on that trip in Europe.
And you never heard high notes.
Oh, that must have -- that must have really given everybody a nosebleed, with Ernie Royal there.

Duke wasn't taking any chances, you see. He had been on that trip over there before and he wasn't taking no chances this time. So Sonny was getting -- he was drinking quite a bit at that time, so he got Butch Ballard as the extra drummer. And that whole trip Sonny hasn't got drunk yet 'cause he didn't want Butch up there playing his drums, you know, playing his gig, of overshadowing him. And it was

a beautiful trip.
That's when I started to playing the plunger. Tyree
didn't go either. So that's when I really starting to playing
the plunger and from then on I had Tricky Sam's chair.
